title: Topology-aware peer balancing, async kernel dispatch, and KV-cache coalescing
author: Lina Ortega
release_notes: Improves multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput and tail latency by introducing topology-aware peer selection, dynamic peer balancing, asynchronous kernel dispatch with stream priorities, and KV-cache request coalescing. No API changes. Rollout gated behind feature flag 'tp_topo_pb'.
description: Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads suffer from suboptimal collective placement and small-KV churn when requests are micro-batched across heterogeneous racks. This PR implements three coordinated runtime optimizations to improve throughput and tail latency: (1) topology-aware peer balancing: build NVLink/NIC-aware ring/graph membership using a lightweight port-speed probe so collectives prefer intra-node/NVLink lanes and minimize cross-node hops, and dynamically rebalance peer pairs when per-step bandwidth estimates indicate hotlinks; (2) async kernel dispatch: move per-layer kernel launch to a dispatch thread pair that annotates CUDA streams with priority and orders kernels for overlap with NCCL comms, and add a non-blocking enqueue-locality check so compute work can start as soon as required dependencies are queued; (3) KV-cache coalescing at the request router: group concurrent small KV reads into coalesced bulk fetches and fold redundant cache population work to reduce memory traffic and small-launch overheads. Design notes: peer selection runs at model load and is re-evaluated when topology events are seen (PCIe/NVLink health changes, new GPUs added). Peer balancing uses a lightweight EWMA of measured pairwise bandwidths to pick an alternating pairing sequence for each micro-batch window. Async dispatch uses two prioritized CUDA streams per device (compute_high, compute_low) plus a comm stream; we rely on CUDA stream priorities instead of artificial host sleeps which reduces scheduling jitter. KV coalescer is conservatively enabled behind the feature flag tp_topo_pb and has a max-coalesce window (configurable) to avoid added latency for single-request critical paths. Implementation summary: runtime/scheduler: add TopologyProbe and PeerBalancer modules, extend DeviceResources to expose stream priorities; runtime/comm: new TopoRingBuilder that prefers NVLink edges, updates NCCL unique IDs to include pairing hints; runtime/dispatch: KernelDispatcher refactor, introduce DispatchFence for dependency tracking and switch to cudaLaunchKernelAsync for fused kernels; router/kv_cache: RequestCoalescer layer with in-process batching and de-duplication. Compatibility and safety: fallbacks to previous ring builder when topology probe fails or when running on unsupported drivers; coalescer has a conservative timeout and a per-model opt-out. Tests and validation: microbenchmarks using benchmark-lab show 18-25% throughput improvement on 8xA100 NVLink topology for half-precision decode workloads with 2048 seq; 95th percentile tail latency reduced by ~14-20% for 8k token streams when KV coalescing is enabled. Perf canary across 3 dedicated clusters showed stable error rates and no observable degradation in output quality. Rollout plan: feature-flagged in main, staged canary to dedicated-qa, then incremental ramp to production Dedicated pools over 72 hours with monitoring on NCCL error counters, GPU PCIe errors, end-to-end latency SLOs. Observability: emit metrics peer_balance/pair_changes, topo_probe/latency_ms, kvcoalesce/coalesce_rate, dispatcher/stream_stall_ms, and add tracing spans for coalescer windows. Documentation: updated runtime/README and redwood-docs/perf for recommended config knobs. CI and perf runs: included unit tests for peer balancer invariants and integration tests in perf-harness. This change is primarily internal runtime improvements; no user API changes expected.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Can you describe failure modes when NVLink bandwidth is asymmetric? Recommended adding an EWMA and a cooldown window.
Lina Ortega: Responded that EWMA already in PeerBalancer and added cooldown; included comment in code and unit tests to validate cooldown behavior.
Priya Nair: Suggests adding a config toggle to limit coalesce window for low-latency flows; asked for a perf run showing single-request latency impact.
Lina Ortega: Added per-model opt-out and microbench that shows median single-request latency increase <1ms with coalesce window set to 2ms.
Lucas Meyer: Code review: requestCoalescer locking looks fine but suggest avoiding blocking on IO thread; recommended converting the final flush to a thread-pool callback.
Lina Ortega: Implemented thread-pool flush and re-ran CI; updated tests.

notes: Hotfix/backout plan: feature flag allows immediate rollback; also added a health-check that will auto-disable peer balancing if NCCL errors exceed threshold. Monitoring dashboard created in observability-pack for rapid rollback.
